newsitem.title: UK: Banish IRA from talks, says murder bid survivor.
newsitem.headline: Banish IRA from talks, says murder bid survivor.

text.p: A politician who escaped a suspected IRA assassination bid urged Britain on Saturday to ditch any plans for the guerrillas to have a voice in Northern Ireland peace talks.

Nigel Dodds, whose police bodyguard was wounded in last month's attack inside a children's hospital, said that any new Irish Republican Army truce would be bogus and simply designed to get its Sinn Fein political wing into talks and further their aim of ending British rule.

"What Sinn Fein and the IRA have been about since day one is peace on their terms," Dodds, who is secretary of the Protestant Democratic Unionist Party (DUP), said ahead of a new round of inter-party talks in Belfast on Monday.
Britain says the IRA must declare a genuine ceasefire as a passport for Sinn Fein into all-party talks but the guerrillas this week signalled their intention to fight on.
"Of course they will have a ceasefire if they believe that that ceasefire will bring (British) concessions and will advance their political agenda," Dodds said in a BBC radio interview.

"Let us make it clear that Sinn Fein/IRA have excluded themselves completely and utterly for any prospect of involvement and let the constitutional democratic parties get on with discussing the real issues," he said.
The IRA called off a 17-month ceasefire almost a year ago, blaming a British refusal to bring them into all-party talks

The talks, which resume on Monday, started in June under former U.S.senator George Mitchell. They are aimed at exploring ways of reviving peace hopes but rival parties say the chances of success are slim.
The DUP suspects that Britain and Ireland want to placate the IRA and put the province on the road to a united Ireland.

Seamus Mallon, deputy leader of the Catholic moderate Social Democratic and Labour Party, accused Protestant "Unionist" parties of sabotaging the talks and said Britain and Ireland must step in to give them more impetus.

Mallon, whose party wants the IRA to declare a truce, said he wanted to see Sinn Fein taking part in the talks "because it is only in that type of negotiating context that we will ever know if they are serious about...a complete end to violence."
In December IRA gunmen wounded Dodds's police bodyguard while the politician was in hospital visiting his gravely ill seven-year-old son.
The IRA denied it was an assassination attempt on the politician but security sources dismissed the disclaimer.
